entries.subject: DAMIT 3233: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-3233.txt. Model 3233, version 2019-05-07, pole (150°, 17°), period 13.1771 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 147.05 ± 3.58 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 47 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: Resolved-model surveys: body-specific candidate not established
entries.finding: The imported survey cites Hanuš 2017, Viikinkoski 2017 and Vernazza 2021 without identifying a selected product for this body. The current DAMIT reference join does not bind selected model 3233 to those surveys. This does not prove that no resolved model exists elsewhere; a body-specific candidate and its release must be identified before the entry can count as included.
entries.revisitWhen: A target row, supplementary model or release URL from one of these surveys establishes a concrete candidate and permits comparison with the selected shape.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 3234, pole ['327', '12'], [Model 3234](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/3234) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 3234: pole (327°, 12°), 13.17707 h, version 2019-05-07. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "73.525 km (approximate thermal scale)" (akari-acua-v1) implies a diameter of 147.05 km, outside the added Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 43, DAMIT model 3233 diameter 133 ± 3 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 3233 fitted to 4 occultations). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed. All 1 Baer et al. mass rows are excluded by the rule (flagged, secondary, or under three times their uncertainty).
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.

entries.subject: Aglaja whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 21 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.951 at 462 nm, 0.989 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#51514e in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 8.2% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.5%), from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2014, ApJ 791, 121; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
